name: UpperTheory.V.PropA.detFactor
source: ∀ (K : Type) [Field K] [IsAlgClosed K] (n : ℕ) (S : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) K),
∃ z : Fin n → K, ∀ c : K, (c • S - 1).det = ∏ i, (c * z i - 1) := by
have hprod : (p.roots.map (fun a => Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C a)).prod = p :=
have hcard : Multiset.card p.roots = n := by
have heval : ∀ x : K, (Matrix.scalar (Fin n) x - S).det = (p.roots.map (fun a => x - a)).prod := by
have hz : ∃ z : Fin n → K, ∀ f : K → K, (p.roots.map f).prod = ∏ i, f (z i) := by
obtain ⟨L, hL⟩ : ∃ L : List K, (L : Multiset K) = p.roots := ⟨_, Multiset.coe_toList _⟩
have hlen : L.length = n := by rw [← hcard, ← hL, Multiset.coe_card]
refine ⟨fun i => L.get (Fin.cast hlen.symm i), fun f => ?_⟩
· have hmat : c • S - 1 = (-c) • (Matrix.scalar (Fin n) c⁻¹ - S) := by
rw [hmat, Matrix.det_smul, heval, hz, Fintype.card_fin, ← Fin.prod_const, ← Finset.prod_mul_distrib]
show: For every algebraically closed field K and every square matrix S of order n over K there are z₁,…,zₙ in K such that for every c ∈ K, det(cS − I) = ∏ᵢ(czᵢ − 1). Multiplicities are included.
strategy: Enumerate the roots of the monic characteristic polynomial and evaluate it at c⁻¹ when c is nonzero.

steps.claim: For the n by n matrix S over the algebraically closed field K, take p(T) = det(TI − S), its characteristic polynomial.
steps.snippet:
∃ z : Fin n → K, ∀ c : K, (c • S - 1).det = ∏ i, (c * z i - 1) := by
  intro K _ _ n S
  classical
  set p := S.charpoly with hp

steps.claim: The characteristic polynomial p of S is monic. Its leading coefficient is one, also for the constant polynomial p = 1 when n = 0.
A monic polynomial over K splits into the product of T − a over its multiset of roots a. Thus this product equals p, with each root repeated according to its multiplicity.
steps.snippet:
have hprod : (p.roots.map (fun a => Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C a)).prod = p :=
    Polynomial.prod_multiset_X_sub_C_of_monic_of_roots_card_eq hmon IsAlgClosed.card_roots_eq_natDegree

steps.claim: In an algebraically closed field the number of roots of a nonzero polynomial counted with multiplicity equals its degree. Since the characteristic polynomial of S has degree n, the root multiset of p has cardinality n.
steps.snippet:
have hcard : Multiset.card p.roots = n := by
    rw [IsAlgClosed.card_roots_eq_natDegree, hp, Matrix.charpoly_natDegree_eq_dim, Fintype.card_fin]

steps.claim: For each x in K, evaluating p(T) = ∏ₐ(T − a) gives det(xI − S) = ∏ₐ(x − a), where a runs over the roots with multiplicity.
steps.snippet: have heval : ∀ x : K, (Matrix.scalar (Fin n) x - S).det = (p.roots.map (fun a => x - a)).prod := by
steps.typedFact: ∀ x : K, (Matrix.scalar (Fin n) x - S).det = (p.roots.map (fun a => x - a)).prod

children.claim: The determinant det(xI − S) is p(x). Evaluation is a ring homomorphism, so it distributes over the root multiset product and sends each polynomial factor T − a to x − a.
children.snippet:
intro x
    rw [← Matrix.eval_charpoly, ← hp]
    conv_lhs => rw [← hprod]
    rw [Polynomial.eval_multiset_prod, Multiset.map_map]
    congr 1
    apply Multiset.map_congr rfl
    intro a _
    simp

steps.claim: There is one enumeration z₁,…,zₙ of the roots such that for every function f from K to K the multiset product of f(a) equals ∏ᵢ f(zᵢ). Enumerating any list representing the root multiset gives this identity with multiplicities.
steps.snippet: have hz : ∃ z : Fin n → K, ∀ f : K → K, (p.roots.map f).prod = ∏ i, f (z i) := by
steps.typedFact: ∃ z : Fin n → K, ∀ f : K → K, (p.roots.map f).prod = ∏ i, f (z i)

children.claim: Choose a list L representing the roots of p. Forgetting the order of a list for this multiset recovers exactly the original roots with their multiplicities.
children.snippet: obtain ⟨L, hL⟩ : ∃ L : List K, (L : Multiset K) = p.roots := ⟨_, Multiset.coe_toList _⟩
children.typedFact: ∃ L : List K, (L : Multiset K) = p.roots

children.claim: The list L has length n because its length equals the cardinality of its multiset, already computed to be n.
children.snippet: have hlen : L.length = n := by rw [← hcard, ← hL, Multiset.coe_card]

children.claim: For each index i take zᵢ to be the corresponding entry of L. For any f the list with entries f(zᵢ) agrees entry by entry with L after applying f, so their products equal the multiset product of the f(a).
children.snippet:
refine ⟨fun i => L.get (Fin.cast hlen.symm i), fun f => ?_⟩
    rw [← hL, Multiset.map_coe, Multiset.prod_coe, ← List.prod_ofFn]
    congr 1
    apply List.ext_get <;> simp [hlen]

steps.claim: Fix the enumeration zᵢ furnished by the product identity. Its validity for every function of a root allows the same enumeration for every scalar c.
steps.snippet:
obtain ⟨z, hz⟩ := hz
  refine ⟨z, fun c => ?_⟩

steps.claim: If c = 0 both sides are (−1)^n. If c ≠ 0, factor −c out of cS − I and evaluate p at c⁻¹. This gives (−c)^n ∏ᵢ(c⁻¹ − zᵢ) = ∏ᵢ(czᵢ − 1). At n = 0 both determinant formulas and the empty product give one.

children.claim: At c = 0 the matrix is −I, whose determinant is (−1)^n. Each of the n scalar factors is −1, so the product is the same.

For c ≠ 0 one has cS − I = (−c)(c⁻¹I − S). Taking determinants and evaluating the split characteristic polynomial yields (−c)^n ∏ᵢ(c⁻¹ − zᵢ). Pairing one copy of −c with each factor gives ∏ᵢ(czᵢ − 1).
children.snippet: · have hmat : c • S - 1 = (-c) • (Matrix.scalar (Fin n) c⁻¹ - S) := by

children.claim: The scalar factorization cS − I = (−c)(c⁻¹I − S) holds entry by entry because cc⁻¹ = 1.
children.snippet: · have hmat : c • S - 1 = (-c) • (Matrix.scalar (Fin n) c⁻¹ - S) := by

children.claim: Equality of matrices follows from equality of all their entries. In position (i,j), the two expressions are cSᵢⱼ − δᵢⱼ and −c(c⁻¹δᵢⱼ − Sᵢⱼ), where δᵢⱼ is the entry of the identity matrix.
On the diagonal the identity matrix contributes one and the equality uses cc⁻¹ = 1. Off the diagonal its entry is zero and both expressions reduce to cSᵢⱼ.
At i = j, the right entry is −c(c⁻¹ − Sᵢᵢ) = cSᵢᵢ − 1, which is the left entry.
children.snippet:
· subst hij
        simp [Matrix.sub_apply, Matrix.one_apply]
        field_simp
        ring

children.claim: At i ≠ j, the scalar matrix c⁻¹I and the identity matrix both have zero entry. Hence the right entry is (−c)(−Sᵢⱼ) = cSᵢⱼ, equal to the left entry.
The determinant of a scalar multiple contributes (−c)^n, and det(c⁻¹I − S) is the product of the c⁻¹ − zᵢ. Since c ≠ 0, each paired factor (−c)(c⁻¹ − zᵢ) equals czᵢ − 1, giving the required product.
children.snippet:
rw [hmat, Matrix.det_smul, heval, hz, Fintype.card_fin, ← Fin.prod_const, ← Finset.prod_mul_distrib]
    refine Finset.prod_congr rfl (fun i _ => ?_)
    field_simp
    ring

chapterTitle: Twisted cokernels in a cyclotomic tower
